Labware for the technique (PCR setup): 2 findings.
1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 38:  p20.dispense(12.5, plate[well])
   The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it
     is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [c750e3fb3380]
2. NOTE LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: master mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
   line 23:  reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix, volume=300)
   Line 23 declares 300 ul of master mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot
     4, load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). The request (PCR setup) puts its reagents in
     tubes, or at a temperature, and a reservoir channel is neither: 300 ul spread over the
     channel is 1.2 mm deep, open to the air and at room temperature, so it warms and
     evaporates while the run goes on, and the tip may not reach it.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Put master mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a
     tube block), not in a reservoir channel.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [4e7cd9721eed]

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 37:  p20.aspirate(12.5, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 37 the p20_single_gen2 draws 12.5 ul from master mix (well A1 in slot 4) with its
   tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 188 ul, which in this NEST
   12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws
   air (this line did it 15 times, after 9 times in the liquid; 188 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 15 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells B4, B5, B6, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [e998b89baca4]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 43:  p20.aspirate(10.5, reservoir["A2"])
   At line 43 the p20_single_gen2 draws 10.5 ul from water (well A2 in slot 4) with its tip
   1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 13 times, after 11 times in the liquid; 136 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 13 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 4.
   Also reached 13 other wells: wells B6, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, D1 and 5 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [02a5b65bff0c]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 11 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 7 more went in (8 to 16% of the well)
   line 50:  p20.dispense(2, plate[well])
   At line 50 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 7 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 3 more in slot 3, which already held master mix and water
   (this line did it 11 times). The addition was 8 to 16% of the well, nothing mixed the
   well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix
   it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 3 more in slot 3 after line 50:
   `mix_after=(5, 10 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 10 to 20, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [f80b687c74c8]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 9 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 38:  p20.dispense(12.5, plate[well])
   At line 38 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   3), and 9 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 1 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 1 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [3ff4734d8a02]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 37 the p20_single_gen2 draws 12.5 ul from master mix (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 188 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 15 times, after 9 times in the liquid; 188 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 15 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
